problem.name: Turaev–Viro invariant
problem.statement_latex: Given a closed 3-manifold by a genus-$g$ Heegaard splitting and a length-$m$ mapping-class word, estimate its Turaev--Viro invariant for a fixed allowed category to additive error $\varepsilon\mathcal D^{2(g-1)}$, with $\mathcal D$ the total quantum dimension.
problem.statement_text: Given a closed 3-manifold by a genus-$g$ Heegaard splitting and a length-$m$ mapping-class word, estimate its Turaev–Viro invariant for a fixed allowed category to additive error $\varepsilon\mathcal D^{2(g-1)}$, with $\mathcal D$ the total quantum dimension.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(g,m,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ gates for failure probability $\delta$ by Alagic--Jordan--Konig--Reichardt, through mapping-class representations.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(g,m,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ gates for failure probability $\delta$ by Alagic–Jordan–Konig–Reichardt, through mapping-class representations.

classical.headline_latex: Classical state-sum or tensor-network contraction is exponential in the presentation width; the normalized approximation is $\mathsf{BQP}$-complete for the specified $SU(2)_k$ and $SO(3)_k$ theories. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.
